architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: The uncertainty probe establishes whether a subsequent dual-axis 120 °C performance-mitigation experiment can be interpreted as a formulation effect rather than an uncontrolled stoichiometric or realization-state change.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Proceed to a modifier-containing candidate only if all of the following are completed before observing modifier performance: verified AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content, moisture specification, and reactive-solids basis; one explicit and reproducible choice between E2-core dilution and MDI adjustment, with resulting candidate NCO/OH calculated; all preparation and measurement-history fields frozen; a numerical initial-viscosity handling range and quantitative replicate-disagreement and trajectory-acceleration rules preregistered; and at least two independently prepared E2-anchor controls plus a contemporaneous qualified reference successfully measured under those frozen rules. Any reconstructed SI midpoint thresholds must be labeled conservative decision rules rather than validated performance limits. If these conditions pass, S1C41 is the leading performance candidate unless new independent pre-result evidence changes tackifier-dose support.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Do not proceed to a performance claim if any modifier functionality, moisture, reactive-solids, stoichiometric-treatment, process-history, handling-range, repeatability-rule, or mandatory-control requirement remains unknown; if independent controls fail the preregistered repeatability or state-control limits; or if the modified-chemistry calibration would be assumed without verification.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Uncertainty qualification before any modifier result, including a 120 °C E2/control hold at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min and an in-range 80-130 °C calibration check or justified subset

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Leading performance-mitigation candidate after uncertainty resolution: it activates both supported axes, uses 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier within the broad supported region, and places TK100 at 5 wt% within the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier cluster. It is not run now because modifier reactivity, stoichiometric treatment, and process-state controls are unresolved.

Lower total modifier burden than S1C41, but its 2.5 wt% TK100 dose is below the supplied 3-10 wt% broad region and repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. Minimum modifier burden cannot break the tie before tackifier-dose sufficiency and comparable evidence coverage are established.

Useful acrylic-only mechanistic control, but it zeroes the independently supported tackifier-like axis. It would be appropriate for causal isolation, not as a replacement for the declared full performance-mitigation experiment.

The E2 reactive-core control is suitable for process-repeatability and state-control qualification within the uncertainty probe, but it does not test either supported modifier axis and therefore is not a performance candidate.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The measured local failure mode is continuing viscosity growth during a 120 °C hold: E1 gave SI15-60 approximately 0.095 and SI15-90 approximately 0.168, whereas E5 gave approximately 0.515 and 0.931. Local temperature sweeps showed ordinary monotonic thermal thinning, and E2 showed large run-to-run viscosity-scale variation; therefore static viscosity, temperature response, hold drift, and realization state must be adjudicated separately. The locally derived rheological rule is that an in-range state anchor can locate realizations on a shared thermal-response shape within the original chemistry family, but this rule has not been shown transferable to modified chemistry and cannot replace a matched hold measurement. The supplied paper and patent evidence supports only directional formulation rules: acrylic-like modification is plausible over a broad 15-25 wt% region, minor tackifier use is plausible over about 3-10 wt% with repeated examples near 5 wt%, and longer-window stability literature confirms that hot-hold drift is a distinct objective. Those sources do not predict the held-out local result, establish an exact optimum, validate the proposed local SI thresholds, or identify a molecular mechanism. Conservative experimental-design constraints introduced here are mandatory contemporaneous state control, frozen preparation history, verified reactive-group and moisture data, an explicit stoichiometric treatment, preregistered handling and repeatability rules, and a replicated 120 °C matched-window hold. These resolve the Skeptic's objections concerning unsupported 2.5 wt% tackifier coverage, premature minimum-burden tie-breaking, unknown NCO/OH, optional controls, unverified calibration transfer, and post-hoc criteria. They also resolve the Robustness Adjudicator's fragile-ranking objection: S1C40 is not selected merely for lower burden, while S1C41 remains the leading full-coverage performance candidate only after interpretability conditions are met. The no-intervention E2 control may be used inside the uncertainty probe, explicitly instead of—not as—the full mitigation experiment. Because the unresolved stoichiometric and process-state uncertainties could make a modifier result uninterpretable, the scientifically useful decision is to freeze an uncertainty-resolution package before selecting a formulation candidate.

evidence_coverage.note: External evidence supports a broad acrylic-like region of 15-25 wt% and a minor-tackifier region of 3-10 wt%, with repeated tackifier examples near 5 wt%. These regions support candidate-family selection, not an exact property prediction.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: This is the required canonical first action. It will establish whether formulation-only or state-aware interpretation is supported, whether one-point state calibration is necessary, how the state-shift master curve and apparent temperature-sensitivity coordinate should be used, and which measurements are required without exposing validation information.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the full measured low-drift reference trajectory and deterministic descriptors so the next experiment can be compared against an original stability benchmark over the same measured 120 °C, 15-90 min window.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the full measured high-drift trajectory defining the failure mode; trajectory shape may distinguish an early offset from continuing drift and therefore affects adjudication.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Verify the declared reactive-core anchor, component fractions, modifier baselines, and MDI fraction before applying acrylic-like or tackifier-like additions; this is needed to keep chemistry changes separate from stoichiometric changes.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After establishing the local objective, obtain the auditable mapping from blinded candidate IDs to the E2-anchored acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes, including the historical and claim boundaries, so one bounded performance-mitigation point can be selected without treating candidate order as rank.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: 120 °C hold stability over 15-60 min and 15-90 min, using SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 and primary loss abs(SI)
Shape and monotonicity of the full hold trajectory, including evidence of continuing acceleration versus a bounded early shift
Initial viscosity at the hold temperature as a processability guardrail, reported only in preserved source units
Viscosity-temperature response within 80-130 °C, including local apparent temperature sensitivity rather than unsupported extrapolation
State-calibrated versus uncalibrated viscosity position, conditional on the master-curve result
Repeat/run variability under controlled preparation and measurement history
Acrylic-like modifier fraction and its distance from externally supported broad analogue regions
Tackifier-like modifier fraction and compliance with the conservative at-or-below-10 wt% boundary
Combined-modifier loading and distance from the E2 reactive-core-only control
Modifier functionality or reactive-group density where known, without inferring it from rheology
NCO/OH stoichiometry, MDI fraction, reactive-solids basis, and whether modifier addition dilutes or changes the reactive core
Compatibility, phase homogeneity, and practical mixing/handling feasibility
Process-history sensitivity, including preparation, moisture exposure, aging, heating, and hold timing
Evidence type for each design choice: directly commensurate local measurement, directional/noncommensurate external evidence, or conservative extrapolation control
counterfactual_checks: Compare the selected modifier-containing point conceptually with the E2 reactive-core-only option to test whether predicted benefit depends on adding modifiers rather than merely reusing the anchor.

Check neighboring single-axis candidates in the blinded lattice before choosing a combined point: acrylic-only neighbors test whether the tackifier is necessary, and tackifier-only neighbors test whether acrylic is necessary. These are ranking counterfactuals, not a requirement to run multiple experiments.
Reject any apparent improvement explainable solely by a lower starting viscosity; require reduced dimensionless hold drift or a clearly more favorable full trajectory.
Check whether the recommendation changes after applying state calibration. A rank reversal would indicate that realization state, not composition, controls the decision.
Check whether the recommendation remains inside the supported region when external evidence is treated only directionally rather than as a numerical optimum.

Check whether maintaining constant reactive stoichiometry versus simple total-formulation substitution changes the candidate's interpretation; unresolved differences trigger abstention or an uncertainty-resolution experiment.
Compare conclusions using both SI15-60 and SI15-90 so an early temporary plateau is not mistaken for sustained stability.
Verify that no candidate ID, ordering, or lattice position is interpreted as historical identity, outcome information, or rank.
planner.decision_goal: Select one blinded candidate formulation for a prospective experiment that mitigates the locally observed hot-hold viscosity drift while retaining usable melt viscosity within the measured 80-130 °C domain, with primary adjudication at the established 120 °C, 15-90 min hold condition. Candidate selection must account separately for viscosity level, temperature response, hold stability, and realization/process state.
design_implications: Optimize hold stability directly, using absolute SI over the measured hold window as a primary loss; do not optimize only the initial or nominal viscosity.
Use 120 °C as the principal hold anchor because it is inside the measured temperature support and is the temperature at which the E1/E5 failure contrast was observed.
Retain an initial-viscosity/processability guardrail so an apparently stable candidate is not accepted merely because it begins at an impractically low or high viscosity.

Treat process history and realization state as explicit nuisance variables. If the state-aware summary confirms a common state-shifted master-curve structure and effective one-point calibration, collect a calibrated anchor measurement rather than interpreting run offsets as chemistry effects.

Use E2 only as the declared reactive-core anchor after its composition and stoichiometric basis are inspected; modifier additions must not silently alter NCO/OH balance or reactive-solids interpretation.

A multi-component acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier intervention is admissible in performance-mitigation mode because the two axes have independent directional support, but both must remain within bounded regions: acrylic-like levels are broad analogue anchors rather than exact local optima, and tackifier-like loading should remain at or below the conservative 10 wt% boundary.

External acrylic evidence near 15-25 wt% and tackifier evidence near 5 wt% are directional or analogue-region evidence, not directly commensurate local optima. The comparative low-OH versus high-OH acrylic stability result supports checking modifier functionality, not asserting a local molecular mechanism.
The literature criterion of no more than about 25% rise over 4-10 h is noncommensurate with the local 15-90 min test and must not be converted into a local numerical acceptance threshold.
Freeze the candidate, objective terms, thresholds, process protocol, and adjudication rules before observing any new result.
material_regularities_to_use: All supplied original temperature-sweep runs decrease monotonically in viscosity from 80 to 130 °C; descriptive Andrade fits are generally strong, with R² approximately 0.965-0.998.

E2 has large run-to-run spread at every measured temperature: sample CV is approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratio is approximately 2.80-3.57. A single nominal viscosity therefore cannot be treated as a formulation-only material constant.
Thermal-hold behavior differs strongly between original formulations under the same reported 120 °C window: E1 has modest positive drift, whereas E5 approaches a near doubling by 90 min.
The temperature effect and hold-time effect are distinct responses: reversible-looking thermal thinning across temperature does not establish stability during an isothermal hold.
The viscosity unit is unknown in the supplied local evidence and must remain unknown; local comparisons should use preserved source values and dimensionless hold SI where appropriate.
The state-shift/master-curve result and the value of one-point state calibration must be obtained from the canonical upstream rheology summary before ranking candidates.
planner.physical_failure_mode: The established failure mode is time-dependent viscosity growth during a 120 °C thermal hold, not merely an unfavorable nominal viscosity. The original E5 hold shows substantially larger drift than E1: SI15-60 is approximately 0.515 versus 0.095, and SI15-90 is approximately 0.931 versus 0.168. Temperature sweeps separately show ordinary monotonic thermal thinning, while E2 exhibits large nominal run spread, so thermal response, temporal drift, and realization/process-state variability must not be conflated.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: A frozen, replicated 120 °C hold trajectory at the same 15, 60, and 90 min landmarks used by the original references, preferably retaining all intermediate measured points.
Initial 120 °C viscosity and SI15-60 and SI15-90, with source units preserved and no invented conversion.
At least one independently prepared repeat to separate formulation performance from realization/process-state variability.
A temperature sweep restricted to the established 80-130 °C support, or the minimum calibrated subset justified by the state-aware summary.
A one-point state-calibration measurement if the canonical summary confirms that state shifts dominate nominal run offsets.
Recorded batch age, moisture-control history, mixing order, mixing time, heating profile, equilibration time, sample mass, geometry, and elapsed time from preparation to measurement.
Actual component masses, total-formulation fractions, MDI fraction, hydroxyl or other reactive functionality where available, and calculated NCO/OH basis.
Observations of phase separation, gel particles, skinning, foaming, or other realization failures that could invalidate rheological comparison.
Contemporaneous measurement of an original reference or qualified control when feasible to detect day or instrument state shifts.
uncertainty_triggers: Abstain from candidate ranking if the state-aware summary is unavailable or contradicts the assumed separation between formulation and realization state.
Treat the result as out of domain if the selected candidate requires temperature or time extrapolation beyond 80-130 °C or 15-90 min for the primary claim.
Do not select a candidate if its composition mapping, E2 anchor relationship, or total-formulation basis is unavailable.
Escalate stoichiometric uncertainty if modifier hydroxyl functionality, moisture contribution, or NCO/OH treatment is unknown and could materially change the reactive network.
Escalate process-state uncertainty if independent preparations show spread comparable to the large E2 nominal run spread.
Treat phase separation, gelation, foaming, or failed mixing as a realization/feasibility failure rather than evidence for or against the proposed rheological direction.
Do not claim mitigation if lower absolute viscosity is accompanied by unchanged or worse dimensionless hold drift.
Do not interpret an external percentage as an exact local optimum; evidence near 15-25 wt% acrylic and below 10 wt% tackifier defines bounded search regions only.
Do not infer molecular mechanism from rheology alone, including attributing improvement specifically to acrylic functionality, dilution, phase behavior, or reaction suppression.
Require pre-result freezing of any numerical objective weights or acceptance thresholds; otherwise use an explicitly ordered qualitative decision rule.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The selected candidate mitigates the locally observed hot-hold viscosity-growth failure under matched 120 °C conditions, rather than merely lowering starting viscosity.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: For both independent preparations, require abs(SI15-60) <= 0.305 and abs(SI15-90) <= 0.550, the midpoints between the measured E1 and E5 reference values, with no phase separation, gel particles, skinning, foaming, or failed mixing. Initial viscosity must also satisfy a pre-frozen application or instrument handling range in preserved source units. A stronger low-drift result is achieved if the replicate mean is no worse than the measured E1 benchmarks of 0.095 and 0.168. No mitigation claim is allowed from lower initial viscosity alone.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail if either independent preparation exceeds either primary midpoint threshold, if SI improves only because of an initial-viscosity shift without reduced dimensionless drift, if preparation spread is comparable to the large E2 state variability, if the trajectory shows unresolved continuing acceleration, or if realization/compatibility defects invalidate comparison.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 °C from 15 to 90 min, evaluated at both 60 and 90 min

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Replicated 120 °C hold trajectory with preserved-source-unit viscosity at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min; primary losses are abs(SI15-60) and abs(SI15-90), with initial 120 °C viscosity reported separately as a processability guardrail.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use the 15 min viscosity at 120 °C as the realization-specific state anchor and hold the same geometry, sample mass, heating profile, equilibration, and timing across at least two independently prepared batches. Record mixing order/time, moisture control, batch age, reaction conditions, and elapsed preparation-to-measurement time. Include a contemporaneous qualified original control when feasible. Use an 80-130 °C sweep or justified calibrated subset to check whether the shared thermal-response shape remains applicable; do not use that sweep as a substitute for the hold measurement.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 min, with mandatory 15-60 min and 15-90 min comparisons and all intermediate trajectory points retained

evidence_against: The 15 wt% acrylic evidence is directional and its literature fraction denominator is not verified as exactly commensurate with total formulation.
The 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the directly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, so its support is conservative axis coverage rather than a direct numeric anchor.
No local modifier-containing hold trajectory has yet been measured.
All six major process-history fields are missing.
evidence_for: Contains 15 wt% AC1920 and 2.5 wt% TK100, so it covers both independently supported intervention axes required for the performance-mitigation intent.
Directly interrogates the E5-type 120 °C hold-drift failure mode rather than merely matching a literature composition or static viscosity.
Preserves the relative E2 reactive-core proportions, limiting unnecessary departure from the characterized local core.
The acrylic level is at the conservative lower edge of the externally supported 15-25 wt% family; the tackifier is a deliberately minor perturbation.
Among strong-analogue, full-coverage candidates in the conservative acrylic band, it has the lowest total modifier burden at 17.5 wt%; this is the minimum-sufficient-intervention tie-break.
key_uncertainty: Whether 2.5 wt% TK100 is sufficient to contribute to mitigation.
Whether AC1920 or TK100 contributes NCO-reactive functionality and therefore changes the true NCO/OH basis.
Whether preparation-state variation could be comparable to the large E2 run spread.
Whether the modified formulation remains homogeneous and practically mixable.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This is the smallest strong-support candidate that tests the complete two-axis mitigation strategy. A replicated matched-window hold directly determines whether the modifier family can suppress dimensionless drift without relying on static viscosity or exact literature-anchor proximity.

evidence_against: Its 20 wt% total modifier burden is larger than S1C40 without local evidence that the additional tackifier is necessary.
The 15 wt% acrylic evidence remains directional rather than a directly commensurate total-formulation anchor.
External tackifier examples generally report processability, not matched 15-90 min thermal-hold stability.
Major process-history and stoichiometric information is missing.
evidence_for: Contains 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 and therefore covers both required intervention axes.
The 5 wt% tackifier level lies directly within the externally documented 4.8-6.4 wt% minor-resin cluster.
It tests whether the low tackifier dose in S1C40 would be insufficient against the observed continuing 120 °C viscosity growth.
It remains within the conservative acrylic starting band and below the external tackifier guidance of about 10 wt%.
key_uncertainty: Whether increasing TK100 from 2.5 to 5 wt% improves drift or only shifts initial viscosity.
Compatibility and phase homogeneity at the combined loading.
True reactive stoichiometry after modifier addition.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This is the most defensible tackifier-region robustness point because 5 wt% is directly commensurate with repeated external analogues. It should follow S1C40 if the objective is to determine whether stronger minor-tackifier coverage is needed, but it is not rank-1 because its higher burden is not yet locally justified.

evidence_against: It adds more acrylic than S1C40 without a local dose-response measurement.
The 17.5 wt% level is an interpolation within an externally supported region, not a directly measured external optimum.
The 2.5 wt% tackifier remains below the repeated direct external cluster.
evidence_for: Contains 17.5 wt% AC1920 and 2.5 wt% TK100, preserving full intervention-axis coverage.
It probes whether the lower acrylic boundary selected in S1C40 is insufficient while retaining a minor tackifier perturbation.
The acrylic loading remains within the broad 15-25 wt% analogue-supported family and the total modifier burden remains 20 wt%.
The E2 core proportions remain fixed, supporting interpretation relative to the characterized local chemistry.
key_uncertainty: Whether increased acrylic loading changes hold drift independently of initial viscosity.
Whether modifier functionality materially alters NCO/OH.
Whether the state-shift calibration remains transferable to this modified chemistry.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This candidate provides an acrylic-dose robustness probe while retaining complete axis coverage. It is ranked below S1C40 because candidates within the same broad support class should not gain a large advantage from numerical proximity to external acrylic percentages, and the additional burden is not yet shown to be necessary.

evidence_against: TK100 is zero, so the candidate omits the independently supported minor tackifier-like axis.
Under the deterministic intervention-sufficiency rule, it is partial coverage and cannot be the default rank-1 performance candidate.
It tests attribution more cleanly than performance sufficiency and therefore does not fully implement the mitigation strategy.
Process and stoichiometric uncertainties remain unresolved.
evidence_for: Contains 15 wt% AC1920 on the E2-derived core and directly tests the acrylic-like axis at the conservative lower region.
It would help determine whether TK100 is necessary if run alongside S1C40.
The acrylic-like formulation family has multiple external analogues and directional stability support.
key_uncertainty: Whether any observed response would generalize to the supported combined-modifier strategy.
Whether apparent benefit would reflect lower initial viscosity rather than lower dimensionless hold drift.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: This is an informative mechanistic control for the tackifier contribution, but it should not replace the full-coverage performance experiment because dropping TK100 would obtain a lower modifier burden by omitting an independently supported intervention axis.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 exhibits the established failure mode, with SI15-60 = 0.515 and SI15-90 = 0.931, versus 0.095 and 0.168 for the lower-drift E1 reference under the same 120 °C window.
Measured local evidence: viscosity decreases monotonically from 80 to 130 °C, but this thermal thinning is distinct from isothermal hold drift and cannot substitute for a matched hold-window test.

Derived state-aware rule: a shared thermal-response shape fits the chemistry-audited local family well, while realization state primarily shifts viscosity scale; one 120 °C anchor produced approximately 6-10% pooled multiplicative calibration error.
Measured local evidence: E2 has large run-to-run viscosity spread, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58, so nominal viscosity cannot be interpreted as a formulation-only constant.

External directly commensurate numeric anchors: acrylic-like modifiers occur near 19-20 and 25 wt% of total formulation, and minor tackifier-like resins occur near 4.8-6.4 wt%; these define coarse analogue regions, not local optima.

External directional or noncommensurate evidence: a reported 15% acrylic addition has an uncertain denominator, and the 25 wt% low-OH versus higher-OH acrylic comparison used a much longer hold window and different chemistry; these support a formulation family and functionality check but not a local molecular mechanism.

Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, first compare candidates covering both independently supported axes, then prefer the minimum sufficient modifier burden within that scientifically sufficient class.
Unresolved uncertainty: modifier reactive functionality, moisture contribution, true NCO/OH after modification, and all major preparation-history fields remain unspecified.
Evidence supports a broad formulation region rather than an exact AC1920/TK100 composition; literature-percentage distance is audit metadata rather than a property predictor.
proposer.scientific_target: Prospectively test whether a bounded acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like modification of the E2 reactive core reduces time-dependent viscosity growth during a 120 °C hold, while preserving usable melt behavior and separating composition effects from realization-state shifts.
unresolved_questions: What are the verified hydroxyl or other NCO-reactive functionalities of AC1920 and TK100, and what is the recalculated NCO/OH after their addition?
Should modifiers be treated as simple total-formulation substitution or should MDI be adjusted to preserve a defined reactive stoichiometry?
What application-specific initial-viscosity range should be frozen before observing the candidate result?
Will the state-shift master-curve calibration remain valid after introducing acrylic-like and tackifier-like chemistry?
What mixing order, reaction temperature/time, moisture-control protocol, equilibration, and sample age will be frozen?
Is S1C40 homogeneous and practically handleable at 15 wt% AC1920 plus 2.5 wt% TK100?
Because the evidence identifies only a broad region, should S1C41 or S1C45 be scheduled only after S1C40, or included in a pre-frozen small comparative block?
A molecular explanation for any improvement remains unresolved and must not be inferred from rheology alone.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It retains 15 wt% acrylic and uses the directly supported 5 wt% tackifier level, giving stronger dual-axis coverage at a modestly higher 20 wt% total modifier burden.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A performance-mitigation experiment proceeds after stoichiometry and process controls are resolved.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It is a cleaner single-axis control but omits the independently supported tackifier axis and therefore is not the preferred performance test.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The intent changes from performance mitigation to causal isolation of the acrylic-like axis.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: It minimizes total modifier burden, but currently provides weaker tackifier-axis support than S1C41.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: Independent pre-result support establishes 2.5 wt% TK100 as sufficient, or a prior local dose-response validates that lower dose.

required_conditions: Verify AC1920 and TK100 hydroxyl or other NCO-reactive functionality, moisture specifications, and reactive-solids basis.
Predefine whether modifier addition dilutes the E2 core or requires MDI adjustment to preserve a specified NCO/OH ratio, and report the resulting stoichiometry.
Freeze mixing order and time, reaction temperature and duration, moisture control, heating profile, equilibration, geometry, sample mass, batch age, and preparation-to-measurement time.
Require a contemporaneous qualified original control or equivalent state-control measurement.
Freeze a numerical initial-viscosity handling range in preserved source units before observing results.
Define quantitative replicate-disagreement and continuing-acceleration rules.
Treat the SI midpoint thresholds as reconstructed conservative decision rules rather than validated performance limits.
Verify transferability of the shared temperature-response shape to the modified chemistry and distinguish that calibration from 15 min hold normalization.
Audit provenance of the 2.5 wt% refinement and ranking rule.
If these conditions are met and no independent support for 2.5 wt% TK100 is added, run S1C41 rather than S1C40.

robustness_checks.detail: The proposed 120 °C replicated hold directly tests the measured time-dependent viscosity-growth failure using SI15-60 and SI15-90 rather than relying on initial viscosity.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier-like candidate is appropriate.

S1C40 uses 2.5 wt% TK100, below the stated 3-10 wt% broad tackifier region and the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. S1C41 uses 5 wt% TK100 and remains supported when exact analogue-distance rewards are removed.
S1C40 nominally activates both axes, but its tackifier dose lacks independent numeric support sufficient to establish evidence-supported coverage. S1C41 more defensibly covers both axes.
S1C40 was promoted over S1C41 primarily for lower total modifier burden before comparable evidence coverage or dose sufficiency was established.
Increasing weight on repeated direct tackifier analogues reranks S1C41 above S1C40; the proposed rank therefore depends on a fragile interpretation of 2.5 wt% as sufficient axis coverage.

AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality, moisture contribution, and the choice between simple substitution and MDI adjustment are unresolved, so true NCO/OH and the meaning of a performance result are uncertain.
All major process-history fields are missing, E2 shows large realization variability, and a contemporaneous qualified control is optional rather than mandatory.

The replicated matched-window hold and dimensionless drift metrics are appropriate, but the initial-viscosity range, replicate-spread rule, acceleration rule, and mandatory state control are not frozen quantitatively.

One-point calibration is supported within the original chemistry family, but transfer to AC1920/TK100-modified chemistry is unverified and the 15 min hold value is not automatically equivalent to an independent thermal-curve state anchor.
The Skeptic identified high-severity candidate-support, stoichiometric, and process-state problems sufficient to block acceptance of S1C40 and require uncertainty resolution before a performance run.
No held-out outcome is disclosed, but the 2.5 wt% refinement and ranking implementation were formalized after validation and lack a contemporaneous freeze artifact.

counterfactual_failures: S1C40 is preferred over S1C41 mainly by lower modifier burden even though 2.5 wt% TK100 is outside the supplied supported tackifier region and its sufficiency is unknown.
The proposal has not established that S1C40 and S1C41 have comparable evidence coverage, so minimum burden is not yet a valid tie-break.
A comparison with the E2 core would remain confounded unless reactive stoichiometry, moisture exposure, and process history are matched.
The proposal acknowledges that S1C39 is only a partial-coverage control, but no equivalent caution is applied to the sub-supported tackifier dose in S1C40.
Without a mandatory contemporaneous reference, an apparent improvement or failure could be caused by realization-state shift rather than formulation.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis defines a broad minor-tackifier region of 3-10 wt% and a repeated directly documented cluster of 4.8-6.4 wt%. S1C40 contains 2.5 wt% TK100. Thus the tackifier family has directional support, but this selected dose does not have independent numeric support sufficient to establish intervention coverage.
critical_findings.issue: S1C40 is labeled full coverage even though its 2.5 wt% TK100 dose is below the supplied tackifier-supported region.

critical_findings.evidence: The proposer selects S1C40 because it is the lowest-burden strong-analogue full-coverage candidate, while explicitly identifying whether 2.5 wt% TK100 is sufficient as a key uncertainty. The deterministic rule permits burden minimization only after intervention sufficiency and comparable evidence coverage are established.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 rationale applies minimum-sufficient intervention before sufficiency has been established.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 uses 5 wt% TK100, which lies within the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% external cluster, while retaining the same 15 wt% acrylic level and complete two-axis design. S1C40's lower burden does not compensate for its unsupported tackifier dose.
critical_findings.issue: S1C41 has better-supported tackifier-axis coverage and should outrank S1C40 if a performance experiment is run before local dose-response evidence exists.

critical_findings.evidence: The verified E2 NCO/OH value of 1.8 applies only to the original reactive core. AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality, moisture contribution, and the rule for MDI adjustment versus total-formulation substitution are unknown. The Planner states that unresolved differences between constant-stoichiometry and substitution interpretations trigger abstention or an uncertainty-resolution experiment.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometry is unresolved, making a formulation-performance result potentially confounded.

critical_findings.evidence: E2 has CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.80-3.57. All six major process-history fields are missing for every candidate. A contemporaneous qualified control is only proposed 'when feasible,' although such a control or equivalent process anchor is needed to distinguish formulation effects from day, instrument, and preparation-state shifts.
critical_findings.issue: Process-state control is inadequate relative to the measured realization variability.

critical_findings.evidence: The state-aware summary supports a one-temperature anchor for locating a realization on a shared temperature-response shape within the audited local chemistry family. It does not establish transfer of that calibration to the modified chemistry or show that normalization by the first hold point removes process-history effects on subsequent temporal drift.
critical_findings.issue: The 15 min hold value is being called a state anchor without establishing that it performs the same role as the upstream one-point thermal-curve calibration.

critical_findings.evidence: The limits abs(SI15-60) <= 0.305 and abs(SI15-90) <= 0.550 are arithmetic midpoints between single measured E1 and E5 trajectories. They are not literature-derived limits, replicated local distributions, or application requirements. They may be used only as explicitly labeled conservative decision rules.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance thresholds are reconstructed midpoint rules rather than validated performance limits.

critical_findings.evidence: The plan requires an initial viscosity within a 'pre-frozen application or instrument handling range,' but no numerical range is supplied. This leaves a primary guardrail open to post-result definition.
critical_findings.issue: The initial-viscosity acceptance criterion is not actually frozen.

critical_findings.evidence: Terms such as preparation spread 'comparable to' E2 variability and 'unresolved continuing acceleration' lack pre-specified calculations or thresholds. With only two preparations, these criteria cannot be applied reproducibly without a frozen rule.
critical_findings.issue: Several failure criteria remain qualitative and post-hoc.

critical_findings.evidence: The directly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier examples primarily establish coexistence and melt processability, not matched 15-90 min hot-hold stability. The stability-context comparison is confounded by MDI and other formulation differences. This supports a prospective axis hypothesis, not an established local mitigation effect.
critical_findings.issue: The tackifier evidence is weaker for the measured physical failure mode than the coverage label implies.

interpretability_failures: Unknown AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content prevents calculation of the candidate's true NCO/OH ratio.
The formulation does not specify whether modifier addition is simple dilution or whether MDI is adjusted to preserve reactive stoichiometry.
The process protocol is not frozen despite large measured realization-state variability.
A 15 min hold normalization cannot by itself separate composition effects from preparation-state effects on subsequent drift.
The state-shift model was established within the original chemistry family and has not been shown transferable to AC1920/TK100-modified formulations.
The numerical initial-viscosity/processability range is absent.
Replicate-disagreement and trajectory-acceleration criteria are not operationally defined.

leakage_check.detail: No validation identity or wet-lab outcome is disclosed, and the supplied tools explicitly report outcome-blind operation. However, the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment, and no contemporaneous repository freeze artifact is available. A provenance audit is therefore required to exclude post-validation tuning of the 2.5 wt% refinement or ranking rule.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly targets dimensionless 120 °C hold drift, separates static viscosity from hold stability, retains both 15-60 and 15-90 min comparisons, and recognizes realization-state variability. However, the rank-1 dose choice and execution plan do not yet satisfy the evidence and state-control requirements.

required_corrections: Obtain verified AC1920 and TK100 hydroxyl or other NCO-reactive functionality, moisture specifications, and reactive-solids basis.
Predefine whether modifiers dilute the E2 core or whether MDI is adjusted to preserve a specified NCO/OH ratio; calculate and report the resulting stoichiometry.
Freeze mixing order, mixing time, reaction temperature and duration, moisture-control protocol, heating profile, equilibration, sample mass, geometry, batch age, and preparation-to-measurement time.
Make a contemporaneous qualified original control or equivalent state-control measurement mandatory rather than optional.
Do not classify 2.5 wt% TK100 as evidence-supported full coverage unless independent pre-result evidence for that dose is supplied.

If proceeding directly to a performance candidate after resolving stoichiometry and process controls, rerank S1C41 above S1C40 because its 5 wt% TK100 level lies within the repeated supported cluster.
Label the SI midpoint thresholds explicitly as reconstructed conservative decision rules, not measured performance limits, and justify their intended decision consequences.
Freeze a numerical initial-viscosity handling range in preserved source units before observing results.
Define quantitative replicate-spread and continuing-acceleration rules, including how two preparations are adjudicated.
Separate the 15 min SI normalization from the upstream state-calibration claim and verify whether the shared temperature-response shape transfers to the modified chemistry.
Audit the post-validation grid and fine-refinement provenance to demonstrate that the 2.5 wt% candidate and ranking logic were not tuned to held-out results.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The narrative generally respects the distinction between local measurements and external analogues, but the proposed execution crosses the Planner's uncertainty boundary by ranking a performance candidate before resolving potentially material stoichiometric and process-state uncertainty. The 2.5 wt% tackifier dose is also treated as supported full coverage despite lying below the supplied evidence region.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This is the required canonical first action. It will establish whether formulation-only or state-aware interpretation is supported, whether one-point state calibration is necessary, how the state-shift master curve and apparent temperature-sensitivity coordinate should be used, and which measurements are required without exposing validation information.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: After establishing the local objective, obtain the auditable mapping from blinded candidate IDs to the E2-anchored acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes, including the historical and claim boundaries, so one bounded performance-mitigation point can be selected without treating candidate order as rank.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
